label: Идущий
description: A 10-sentence card for идущий, the present active participle of идти.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine nominative. Идущий comes from идти via the present stem идут plus -щ- and an ending. It agrees with masculine мужчина and means the man who is walking ahead.
Strategic focus: Feminine nominative. The feminine ending -ая lets идущая agree with девушка, marking the girl who is walking down the street.
Strategic focus: Neuter nominative. Идущее takes the neuter ending -ее to match облако, describing the cloud moving toward us.
Strategic focus: Plural nominative. The plural ending -ие joins идущие to дети, picking out the children who are walking home.
Strategic focus: Masculine accusative. With the animate object старика the participle takes -его, so идущего agrees in gender, number and case as the old man I overtook.
Strategic focus: Feminine genitive. Идущей carries the feminine genitive ending to agree with женщины, marking whose steps they are — the steps of the woman walking behind.
Strategic focus: Masculine dative. The dative object другу pulls идущему into the dative -ему ending, naming the friend walking toward me whom I waved at.

missions.phrase: Я иду рядом с идущим солдатом.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine instrumental. After рядом с the noun солдатом stands in the instrumental, and идущим takes the matching instrumental ending to agree with the marching soldier.

missions.phrase: Мы говорим об идущем впереди поезде.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine prepositional. The preposition об governs the prepositional case, so поезде and идущем both take prepositional endings as the train ahead we speak about.

Strategic focus: Plural nominative paraphrase. Идущие на работу люди unfolds as люди, которые идут на работу — people who are walking to work. The participle compresses that который-clause into one agreeing word.
